//: case_16723128 tool_connection registration payload. Substitute MCP_HOSTNAME and
the secretId of the bearer, then create the connection with this config.
THE FIELDS THAT SILENTLY VOID THE TRANSPORT
config.headerPolicy.metadata.forward. The gateway derives its metadata
headers from this list and THE DEFAULT IS THE EMPTY LIST. A connection
registered the obvious way — url and nothing else — sends NO identity
header, with no error, no warning, and no degraded health status. This
transport fails closed on the first tools/call rather than acting
anonymously, but that is a backstop, not a reason to omit this list.
The list MUST contain all four of agent_id, company_id, run_id AND
issue_id. The first three authenticate the caller; issue_id attributes
the host read to the calling card in the broker's audit chain. Without
it every call fails closed on the missing x-paperclip-issue-id.
It must sit under `config`, not `transport_config`. readHeaderPolicy
checks config first and falls back to transportConfig; put it in config
and do not rely on the fallback.
NO SECRET IN THE URL
The bearer is a Paperclip secret, injected as an Authorization header
per call by resolveCredentialHeaders, and must never land in
transport_config.url, activity, invocation or audit logs.
VERSION SELECTOR
Left unset, which resolves to `latest`. Do not pin it: a pinned
versionSelector silently keeps serving the old value through a rotation,
so a rotated-because-leaked bearer would go on working.
name: Host operations broker (Phase-0 reads)
description: Fixed-verb host reads through the host-ops broker: service state, health, tooling location. Identity is taken from the Paperclip tool gateway and is never a tool argument. Phase-0 read verbs only — no writes, deploys or restarts exist on this transport.
